title: The Koszul chain complex is a projective resolution of its quotient
statement: For every commutative ring A, ideal I, natural number r, and sequence f:Fin r -> A which is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] and has span(range f)=I, there exists a projective resolution P of the A-module A/I whose chain complex is exactly K_A(f) [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. No assumption that I is proper or r is positive is made.

source.place: Lemma 48.15.5, finite free Koszul resolution; Tags 0623 and 062E for the augmentation and Koszul regularity

proof.text: Construct the augmentation: identify wedge^0(A^r) with A and then quotient by I in degree zero; use zero in positive degrees. Contraction d_1 sends e_i to f_i, so its image is span(range f)=I and the augmentation is a chain map.

The cokernel universal property identifies the induced map on H_0 with A/I. Positive homology vanishes by Koszul regularity and the target single complex has zero positive homology. Therefore the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

Each Koszul term has the exterior basis of the standard finite free module, hence is free and projective. Bundle the same complex and augmentation as a ProjectiveResolution; its complex field is exactly the given Koszul complex.
